### Observed differences

- The two parallel groups of activities exchanged shares: in the earlier window, A01, A03, A04 and A05 each took part in about 91 of 200 traces while A02, A06, A07 and A08 each took part in about 109; in the later window this reversed to about 106 versus 94 of 200. None of the eight activities repeats within a trace in either window [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008].
- The preferred traversal order within these groups also shifted: from A01, the share continuing to A05 fell from about 41% to 32% of that activity's outgoing transitions while the share to A04 rose from 23% to 31%; A04 passed on to A09 less often (44% to 33%) and A05 more often (31% to 40%); from A02 the share to A07 rose (28% to 39%) and to A08 fell (38% to 24%), with A07→A08 and A08→A06 gaining in step [DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR002, DIR007, DIR008].
- After A41, the split between its successors moved from about 55/45 in favour of A43 to about 47/53 in favour of A42; A42 took part in about 66 of 100 traces after versus 61 before and repeated somewhat more often (0.91 versus 0.77 occurrences per trace), while A43 and A44 receded slightly (about 61 versus 63 of 100 traces) [DIR025, OCC027, OCC028, OCC029].
- Smaller shifts of the same kind appear at other decision points: after A17, continuation to A19 rose from about 22% to 35% of A17's outgoing transitions (A19 now in 56 of 100 traces versus 48, A18 in 44 versus 52); after A39, continuation to A38 rose from 33% to 41% (A38 itself remains uncommon, in about 21 of 100 traces versus 14); after A40, continuation to A14 rose from 30% to 38% while A15 and A20 receded; and the exit to A29 around A36/A37, previously taken more often from A37 (56%) than from A36 (44%), is now taken more often from A36 (54%) than from A37 (46%) [DIR011, OCC017, OCC018, DIR023, OCC024, DIR024, OCC013, DIR021, DIR022, DIR016].
- A10 and A11 occur in every trace in both windows but repeat slightly more often in the later window (about 1.66 versus 1.58 occurrences per trace; repeated in about 41 of 100 traces versus 35) [OCC009, OCC010].
- The remaining listed items are differences of only about 1–4 percentage points, several with low empirical strength and two with practically no difference at all [OCC011, OCC012, OCC015, OCC016, OCC020, OCC021, DIR003, DIR010, DIR027].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The shifts described above are modest (about 3–13 percentage points) and of a size that random re-splits of unchanged data also produce — even the largest single difference is still exceeded by about 4 in 100 of those re-splits, which is unremarkable as the largest value among roughly fifty indicators — while many agreeing items merely restate the same traces (A01, A03, A04 and A05, for example, have identical profiles) and no structural or relational evidence corroborates a real change, so sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows cannot be ruled out [DIR025, OCC001, OCC002, DIR010].
